text: A song of ascents. I lift my eyes to the mountains — where will my help come from?
My help comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth.

versions.text: My help comes from the LORD, the maker of heaven and earth.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew participle עֹשֵׂה functions verbally; a relative clause reads more naturally aloud than the noun phrase "the maker of," and it keeps the rhythm of the short line.

text: He will not let your foot slip; he who watches over you will not slumber.
See, he who watches over Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
The LORD watches over you; the LORD is your shade at your right side.

versions.text: The LORD watches over you; the LORD is your shade at your right hand.
versions.explanation: עַל־יַד יְמִינֶךָ literally means "at your right hand/side"; "shade at your right hand" can sound odd in oral reading since "hand" and "shade" collide. "Right side" preserves the sense of nearness and protection while reading smoothly.

text: The sun will not strike you by day, nor the moon by night.
The LORD will keep you from all harm; he will watch over your life.
The LORD will watch over your going out and your coming in, now and forevermore.

versions.text: The LORD will watch over your going out and your coming in, from this time on and forever.
versions.explanation: "From this time on and forever" is slightly wordy and stumbles when read aloud; "now and forevermore" renders מֵעַתָּה וְעַד־עוֹלָם accurately with a stronger closing cadence for the psalm.
